verdict.rationale: The docs suggest a vision-model approach: screenshots go to an OpenAI-compatible vision endpoint, and a calibrated AssistiveTouch pointer clicks. Misclicks can be debugged by replaying runs with taps and swipes drawn on top, or by exporting traces. The perception and grounding method itself is only implied, not explicitly documented. Missing for 10: an explicit statement of the element-location method (coordinates vs set-of-marks vs OCR vs accessibility tree), documentation of how model output maps to pointer coordinates, and independent corroboration of debugging misclicks.

support.subject: As a developer, the approach to locating UI elements (accessibility tree, OCR, set-of-marks, coordinates) is documented, so misclicks are debuggable

citations.quote: Any OpenAI-compatible vision endpoint works (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, cloud APIs).
turn on AssistiveTouch; the app calibrates the pointer by itself.
replay it step by step with the taps and swipes drawn on top.
Export the screenshots, actions and saved annotations from Runs
The prompts are plain text in prompts/ and bundled with the app
